title: Written asthma action plan completeness at discharge and emergency revisits within 90 days in children: a linked cohort study
abstract: Objective: to estimate the association between a complete written asthma action plan at discharge and asthma emergency revisits or readmissions within 90 days. Design: cohort of first asthma discharges per child from 2022 to 2025 at one children's hospital, linked to provincial emergency visit data. Exposure: five of five plan sections complete. Outcome: first asthma emergency visit or readmission at any provincial hospital. Results and conclusions will be written after linkage and analysis.
introduction: Written action plans reduce urgent care use in trials, but plans are often incomplete in practice, and revisits to other hospitals are invisible to the discharging team. Whether completeness itself matters is unknown for this population.
methods: Plans are scored with a five-item completeness score by educators blind to outcomes. Revisits and readmissions come from the provincial dataset after linkage. A Cox model adjusts for seven pre-specified covariates; injury visits serve as a negative control outcome.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present the cohort flow, completeness by section, events at the discharging and other hospitals, crude and adjusted hazard ratios, the negative control result and the association by language group.
discussion: The discussion will weigh the estimate against the retrieved provincial cohort and the trials of written plans, and consider how much of any association could reflect family engagement rather than the plan itself. It will state what the result means for funding an electronic plan with forced fields.
limitations: Residual confounding by family engagement is likely, and plans missing from the archive may not be missing at random. Revisits outside the province are not captured, and the study covers one children's hospital.
conclusion: To be written after analysis. It will describe an association and will not claim that completeness causes fewer revisits.
summary: STROBE and RECORD structured draft; results left empty until the linked analysis.
